hints: The acceleration changes with time, so v = u + at does not apply. The change in velocity is the area under the a–t graph.
worded:
1. Acceleration grows with time, so the “v = u + at” shortcut is out: it assumes constant a.

2. Change in velocity = area under the a–t graph. Here the graph is a straight line from 0 to αt: a triangle of area ½ × t × αt = ½αt².

3. So v = u + ½αt². (B)

4. Option (A) is what you get by wrongly putting a = αt into v = u + at.
conventional:
![](asset:P000143-sol-1)

$$\frac{dv}{dt} = \alpha t\  \Rightarrow \ \int_{u}^{v}dv = \int_{0}^{t}\alpha t\, dt\  \Rightarrow \ v = u + \frac{1}{2}\alpha t^{2}.$$
mistakes: Putting a = αt into v = u + at gives option (A): wrong, because a is not constant.
